Convectional rain is rain that falls in hot places like Singapore, usually in the afternoon. The sun heats the ground strongly and the ground heats the air above it. The warm air becomes less dense and rises. As it rises it cools, and the water vapour condenses to form clouds. The water droplets in the clouds get bigger and heavier until they fall as rain.

A tsunami is a very big wave that destroys buildings and kills many people living near the sea. An earthquake under the sea makes the sea floor suddenly move upwards. This pushes up a huge amount of sea water above it and forms waves. The waves move very fast across the open sea and are not high there. When they reach shallow water near the coast, they slow down and become much taller, then crash onto the shore.

Volcanoes are mountains that erupt with lava and ash, and the eruptions can be very dangerous for people. The soil near volcanoes is very fertile. The lava and ash break down into soil that is rich in minerals, so farmers can grow more crops. Volcanoes also attract tourists. Visitors come to see the crater and bathe in hot springs, so local people can earn money as guides or by running guesthouses.

Green spaces are parks and gardens. Singapore has many of them and they look beautiful. Residents can use green spaces to exercise and play. For example, they can jog or cycle in the park, which keeps them physically healthy. The trees also cool the neighbourhood.
